queries.hook: I feel lonely. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Loneliness and emptiness come from feeling separate from people, purpose and the divine; the heart is searching for where it belongs.
queries.steady: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.
queries.act: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Before his final words, Krishna tells Arjuna why he is saying them.
hook.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
hook.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
hook.translation: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
alternates.sanskrit: अपि चेदसि पापेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः पापकृत्तमः । सर्वं ज्ञानप्लवेनैव वृजिनं सन्तरिष्यसि ॥
alternates.line: Even if you were the worst wrongdoer of all, the raft of wisdom would carry you across.
alternates.translation: Even if you are the most sinful of all sinners, you will cross over all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.

words.en: by the boat of knowledge alone

alternates.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.
alternates.misuse: Not 'understanding cancels the harm done to others'; it frees you to change and make amends.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
alternates.sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
alternates.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
alternates.translation: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.

words.en: standing in the heart of all beings

alternates.why: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

prasang.title: Krishna describes his glories
prasang.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasang.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Before his final words, Krishna tells Arjuna why he is saying them.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥
verse.line: Listen once more to my deepest word: you are truly dear to me.
verse.translation: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna just before the final teaching of the Gita. He tells Arjuna that he is saying these things because Arjuna is deeply loved by him. The verse means that the deepest and most secret teaching is offered not because Arjuna has earned it, but because Krishna cares for him. It proposes that the most profound guidance is given out of affection, and that being deeply loved is the reason the truth is revealed.
verse.for_you: You are sitting with your books and the room feels quiet, and the distance between you and your friends is growing. The verse says the deepest truth is shared because someone cares. That care is already here, in the very fact that you are reading this.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own waiting room, and the one who cares is already there.
asks: What does it mean to be deeply loved when I feel alone?
How does being loved change the way I study?

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.meaning: The sage Ashma tells King Janaka that sorrow has only two roots: something unwanted happening to you, or your own mind spinning. There is no third source. When people and things leave, days never return. Grieve what is gone, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.
verse.for_you: You feel cut off and unseen, and the silence between you and your friends is heavy. That distance is real. The text says your pain is either the loss or the spinning mind, and you can steady it by seeing who is still there.
verse.try_today: Notice one person who is still in your life and let them be enough.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own quiet room, watching the people you know drift away.
asks: How do I know if my mind is spinning or if something is wrong?
Who is still in front of me right now?
Can I steady myself without forcing it?

verse.speaker: Surdas
verse.setting: Surdas asks to be kept in shelter.
verse.sanskrit: अब मोहि सरन राखिये नाथ ! कृपा करी जो गुरुजन पठए, बह्यो जात गह्यो हाथ ॥
verse.line: Keep me in your shelter now. I was being swept away, and your grace sent people who caught my hand.
verse.translation: Now keep me in your shelter, Lord. By your grace the elders were sent; as I was being swept away, they caught my hand.
verse.meaning: Surdas speaks directly to the Lord. He is being carried off by a flood, and he asks to be kept safe. He says that by the Lord's grace, elders were sent to catch his hand and stop him from being swept away. The verse proposes that a person can be held up by others who act out of grace, and that this rescue is a sign of shelter and care.
verse.for_you: You are in your study and you feel cut off, as if the ground is slipping under you. Yet you are being held. The elders who caught your hand were not strangers. They are the friends and the teacher who stayed near even when the noise grew.
verse.try_today: Notice one person who has stayed near you this week.
verse.scene_line: You are the one being swept away, and they are the ones sent to catch your hand.
asks: How do I know when someone is catching my hand?
What if the hand I see is only a shadow?
Can I ask for the hand to be held tighter?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: One of the best-known verses of the Upanishad, on the God within all.
verse.sanskrit: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥
verse.line: One God is hidden in every being: the inner self of all, the quiet witness of all we do.
verse.translation: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
verse.why: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

prasang.title: Shvetashvatara: from 'what governs our lives?' to refuge
prasang.summary: Seekers ask what causes the world and governs their joys and sorrows. Through meditation they come to see one Lord, Rudra-Shiva, hidden in every heart; the Upanishad moves from inquiry to recognition to a prayer of refuge (6.18) and ends on grace and love of God (6.21, 6.23).
prasang.lesson: Refuge in God comes at the end of honest questioning, not instead of it.

verse.meaning: In the Shvetashvatara Upanishad, seekers ask what governs their joys and sorrows. After honest questioning, the seer tells them that one God is hidden in every being. This is the inner self, the quiet witness of all we do. It is the overseer of every action, dwelling inside everyone. It is pure awareness, alone and beyond all qualities. The verse proposes that this inner presence is the true shelter you can hold onto.
verse.for_you: The verse does not say the people left. It says the witness inside you is always there.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you feel unseen, and simply watch it happen.
verse.scene_line: You are the unseen witness in your own crowded room.
asks: How do I sit with the witness when I feel alone?

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥
verse.line: See yourself in every being and every being in yourself, and you see the same everywhere.
verse.translation: One whose self is joined in yoga sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self; he sees the same everywhere.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.for_you: See yourself in all beings and all beings in yourself; reach out and serve, knowing there is no true distance.

story.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
story.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
story.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
story.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

anchor.speaker: Bhasa
anchor.setting: Two childhood friends meet again in old age; one admits he never found peace.
anchor.sanskrit: उह्यमानमनन्तेषु चेतः कार्यमहोर्मिषु । क्षणमेति न विश्रान्तिं चिन्ताताण्डविताशयम् ॥ इदं कृतं करोमीदं करिष्यामीदमित्यलम् । कलनाजालवलिता मूर्च्छिता मतिपक्षिणी ॥
anchor.line: 'Done this, doing this, must do that.' Caught in endless lists, the mind never gets a moment's rest.
anchor.translation: Carried along on endless great waves of tasks, the mind never gets a moment's rest; its depths dance with worry. 'This I've done, this I'm doing, this I'll do': so the bird of the mind, tangled in a net of reckonings, faints.
anchor.why: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

prasang.title: Two old friends meet again and admit they never found peace
prasang.summary: Bhasa and Vilasa grow up inseparable in a forest hermitage. After their fathers die they drift apart and spend long lonely years in hard austerities. When they meet again as old men, one asks if the other is well; he answers honestly that there is no wellness while the mind keeps spinning through endless tasks and worries.
prasang.story_hook: They had been inseparable as boys, and when they met again they were old men with nothing to show.
prasang.lesson: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.

story.hook_title: Two childhood friends met again as old men, and neither had found peace
story.teaser: Two childhood friends met again as old men, and neither had found peace
story.for_you: Years of hard effort without inner understanding can leave you exactly where you started.
asks: What is the endless list I keep running through?
How do I rest when the mind will not stop?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: the first being, alone.
verse.sanskrit: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Alone, he was afraid. Then he asked: since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?
verse.translation: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

matched.label: I feel anxious most of the time

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

verse.meaning: In the first story of the world, the first being was alone. They were afraid. Then they asked themselves a question. They wondered why they were afraid when there was no one else. They realised their fear came from thinking another being existed. Once they saw there was only themselves, the fear left.
verse.for_you: You feel cut off, as if you are alone in a crowd. That feeling is real. It is not a failure, it is the start of knowing your own ground.
verse.try_today: Notice when you feel unseen and ask what is there.
verse.scene_line: You are the first being, alone, and afraid.
asks: What am I afraid of when no one is near?
How do I stand when I feel alone?

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama, near the end of his lament, says where the real enemy lives.
verse.sanskrit: शत्रवश्चेन्द्रियाण्येव सत्यं यातमसत्यताम् । प्रहरत्यात्मनैवात्मा मनसैव मनो रिपुः ॥
verse.line: No one hurts us like we hurt ourselves. The mind becomes the mind's own enemy.
verse.translation: Our own senses are the enemies; truth itself has turned untrue; the self strikes the self, and the mind is the mind's own enemy.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.
verse.misuse: Not a reason to blame yourself. Vasishtha's answer is that the same mind can lift itself.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: Rama says this to Vishvamitra and Vasishtha while he is still in the middle of his grief. He has just watched his father die and is wondering if anything in life is real or lasting. He looks at his own mind and names what is happening. He says our own senses are the enemies and truth itself has turned untrue. The self strikes the self and the mind becomes the mind's own enemy. He is not saying you are broken.
verse.for_you: You are studying and the people around you feel far away even when they are in the room. That distance is not your fault and it is not your whole story. The mind that feels empty can also be the mind that reaches out.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when your mind feels like it is working against you.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting with your books and your mind turns on itself.
asks: How do I tell the mind's voice from my own?
Can the mind that hurts me also help me?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
verse.sanskrit: यदृच्छालाभसन्तुष्टो द्वन्द्वातीतो विमत्सरः । समः सिद्धावसिद्धौ च कृत्वापि न निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Content with what comes, beyond envy, steady in success and failure, you stay free even while working.
verse.translation: Content with whatever comes unasked, beyond the pairs of opposites, free from envy, the same in success and failure, even when acting he is not bound.
verse.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

prasang.title: How the great yogis live
prasang.summary: The wise act without selfish motive, content and dependent on nothing, free from envy, steady in success and failure.
prasang.lesson: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the wise person works without being tied down. They are content with whatever arrives without asking for it. They do not envy what others have. They remain the same whether they succeed or fail. Even while they are busy doing things, they are free.
verse.for_you: You are studying and feeling like an imposter. That comes from wanting to be seen as worthy by others. The idea here is to work without needing the result. You can sit with your books and give your attention to the task itself.
verse.try_today: Pick one small task and do it without checking for approval or results.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own study, working without needing the outcome to prove you belong.
asks: How do I separate my effort from my need for praise?
Can I find a steady place to stand right now?

verse.speaker: Rahim
verse.setting: Rahim on a love so close it needs no news.
verse.sanskrit: जेहिं रहीम तन-मन दियो, कियो हिए बिच भौन। तासों दुख-सुख कहन की, रही बात अब कौन॥
verse.line: The one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining.
verse.translation: Rahim says: to the one who has been given body and mind, who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling?
verse.meaning: Rahim sits with a love so close it needs no news. To the one who has made a home in the heart, what joy or sorrow is left that needs telling? He says that the body and the mind are given, and the one who lives inside already knows your every feeling. Nothing needs explaining. The verse proposes that the part of you that feels lonely is already seen, held, and known by the presence that lives in your heart.
verse.for_you: The loneliness you feel among your friends is the ache of feeling unseen. But the verse turns the frame: the one who lives in your heart already knows your joys and sorrows. Nothing needs explaining. You can rest in that truth today without needing to perform or prove your place.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you do not need to explain yourself to the mirror.
verse.scene_line: You are in a room full of voices, and the one who lives in your heart already knows your quiet.
asks: How do I feel held when no one here seems to see me?
Can I trust that being known inside is enough for now?
What does it mean to let myself be known without words?

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verse.sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
verse.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verse.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom. They are calm, inquiry, contentment, and good company. He says you only need to start with one. If you pick good company, it will guard your mind and bring the others with it.
verse.for_you: You are waiting for the others to make the first move, but the gate is open. Pick one calm, clear thought and let it stand with you in the library, on the bus, in your room. One quiet mind is company enough, and it will bring the others with it.
verse.try_today: Notice the one calm, clear thought in your mind today.
verse.scene_line: You are at the fourth gate, choosing good company.
asks: How do I find good company when I am alone?
Can one thought really change how I feel?
What does calm company look like for me?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The Isha on seeing one life in all beings.
verse.sanskrit: यस्तु सर्वाणि भूतान्यात्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विजुगुप्सते ॥
verse.line: See yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself, and you stop recoiling from people.
verse.translation: One who sees all beings in the self, and the self in all beings, no longer shrinks away from anyone.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.meaning: The seer of the Isha Upanishad speaks to the reader sitting in the quiet of their own mind. They have just said that everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. Now they add that the way to stop pulling back from others is to see yourself in everyone and everyone in yourself. This means your loneliness is not a lack of people around you. It is a habit of looking at others as separate and judging them.
verse.for_you: You feel unseen in your study group and your classroom, and the gap has grown without anyone saying a word. The Isha tells you that the person you think is separate from you is only your own mind wearing a different face.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own study hall, and the question is who is looking at whom.
asks: How do I see myself in the people I study with?
What does it mean to stop recoiling from my friends?
Can I look at my teacher and see my own face there?

story.title: Sita in captivity
story.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.
story.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
story.lesson: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

anchor.speaker: Sita
anchor.setting: Alone in captivity, Sita fears Ram has forgotten her, then reassures herself.
anchor.sanskrit: दृश्यमाने भवेत् प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यदृश्यतः। नाशयन्ति कृतघ्नास्तु न रामो नाशयिष्यति॥
anchor.line: 'Out of sight, out of mind' is true only of the ungrateful. Real love survives distance.
anchor.translation: Love lasts while someone is in sight; out of sight, affection fades. But that is the way of the ungrateful. Ram will not let it fade.
anchor.why: Hold on to love across distance; hope can arrive from unexpected people.

prasang.summary: Guards threaten Sita day and night. She fears Ram has forgotten her, then reminds herself that out of sight is out of mind only for the ungrateful. The guard Trijata dreams of Ram's victory, and good omens begin to appear.
prasang.story_hook: She had been alone in the grove for ten months, surrounded by guards who mocked her every day.

story.hook_title: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
story.teaser: Ten months alone in Ravana's grove, Sita began to fear Ram had forgotten her
asks: How do I tell the difference between a friend and a guard?
What does Trijata's hope look like in my daily life?
How do I stop waiting for Ram to rescue me?

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call feeling cut off, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.insight: Even among people, you've felt unseen, and the distance has grown without anyone saying so.

queries.hook: I feel lonely. Inside, something doesn't sit right and I can't name it, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Loneliness and emptiness come from feeling separate from people, purpose and the divine; the heart is searching for where it belongs.
queries.steady: You belong more than you feel right now; the people and the practice that hold you are still within reach.
queries.act: Reach out to the people and the practice that hold you; seek good company, and remember you are never truly alone.
queries.story: A story of a husband and wife, facing feeling cut off.

understanding.life_context: Studying. Feels uneasy; closest to "I feel lonely" and "I feel like an imposter".

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna names the chief glories in which the divine shows itself.
verse.sanskrit: अहमात्मा गुडाकेश सर्वभूताशयस्थितः । अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भूतानामन्त एव च ॥
verse.line: I am the self seated in every heart: the beginning, middle and end of all beings.
verse.translation: I am the self, Gudakesha, seated in the hearts of all beings. I am the beginning, the middle and the end of beings.

words.en: standing in the heart of all beings

verse.why: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

prasang.title: Krishna describes his glories
prasang.summary: Krishna lists his manifestations: among lights the sun, among rivers the Ganga, and ends by saying any excellence is a spark of his splendour.
prasang.lesson: Whatever excellence you admire is a spark of the divine.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that the divine is not somewhere far away. It is seated right in the heart of every living being. It is the start and the finish of everything that exists. This means that any quality you see in the world, any skill, any beauty, any strength, is just a small spark of that same source. The excellence you admire is not separate from you. It is a piece of the same whole.
verse.for_you: You are sitting in a room full of people but the space between you feels wide and empty. You see your friends laughing and you feel like an outsider looking in. The verse says that the same spark that makes your friends shine is also inside you.
verse.try_today: Notice one small skill or quality in a friend and let it be a mirror for your own spark.
verse.scene_line: You sit in the common room, a heart among many, unseen.
asks: How do I see the same spark in me that I see in others?
What if I am not separate from the group but part of it?
How do I stop measuring my worth by their reaction to me?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्ताभिमानी मुक्तो हि बद्धो बद्धाभिमान्यपि । किंवदन्तीह सत्येयं या मतिः सा गतिर्भवेत् ॥
verse.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.
verse.translation: One who thinks 'I am free' is free, and one who thinks 'I am bound' stays bound. The saying here is true: as you think, so you become.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.
verse.misuse: This is about inner freedom; it does not deny real constraints or problems that need action.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free. Ashtavakra answers that your belief about yourself shapes your reality. If you believe you are free, you are free. If you believe you are bound, you remain bound. Your thinking is what makes you what you are.
verse.for_you: The loneliness you feel and the fear of being an imposter are beliefs you are carrying about yourself. You are not your exam results or your friends' attention. You are the awareness that watches them. You can believe you are worthy and you are.
verse.try_today: Notice when you feel like an imposter and tell yourself you are free.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own classroom, and the question is how you see yourself.
asks: How do I know if I am free or just pretending?
Can I change how I see myself just by thinking differently?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on nature and spirit, and seeing the same self in all.
verse.sanskrit: यथा सर्वगतं सौक्ष्म्यादाकाशं नोपलिप्यते । सर्वत्रावस्थितो देहे तथाऽऽत्मा नोपलिप्यते ॥
verse.line: Like the sky, untouched by everything that moves through it, the self stays unstained.
verse.translation: As the all-pervading sky, because of its subtlety, is not stained, so the self, present in every body, is not stained.
verse.why: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

prasang.title: Nature and spirit
prasang.summary: Nature does the acting; the self witnesses. Some reach the truth by meditation, some by reason, some by work, some by listening. Whoever sees the same divine in all beings stops harming themselves.
prasang.lesson: See the same presence in everyone and you stop wounding yourself.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the self is like the sky. The sky is vast and subtle, and nothing that moves through it can leave a stain. The same is true for the self inside every body. It is present everywhere, but it remains untouched by whatever happens around it. The point is that if you see the same presence in everyone, you will stop wounding yourself.
verse.for_you: You sit in a room full of people and still feel the distance. The texts say the self inside them is the same as the self inside you, untouched by the noise. You do not have to earn their attention to be real.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when the room feels neutral instead of empty.
verse.scene_line: You are in a room where everyone moves and the sky inside them stays clear.
asks: How do I know if I am seeing the same self in them?
Can I feel this sky when I am alone?

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra presses home his core teaching to Janaka: you are awareness, not the roles you play.
verse.sanskrit: गुणैः संवेष्टितो देहस्तिष्ठत्यायाति याति च । आत्मा न गन्ता नागन्ता किमेनमनुशोचसि ॥
verse.line: The body comes and goes; what you truly are does not. Why grieve so?
verse.translation: The body, made of nature's qualities, comes, stays and goes. The Self neither comes nor goes. Why grieve for it?
verse.why: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.
verse.misuse: Grief is natural; this offers perspective, not a rule against mourning.

prasang.title: You are not your mind
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra drives home that Janaka is not the body, the doer, or the mind's likes and dislikes, but the ocean in which the waves of life rise and fall. He urges faith, an end to grief, and rest from endless deliberation.
prasang.lesson: You are the ocean, not the waves; let them rise and fall without losing yourself.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra speaks to Janaka, who is caught in the weight of his role and the fear of loss. The sage points to the truth that the physical body, shaped by nature's forces, is merely a temporary visitor that arrives and departs. The Self, however, is the eternal witness that neither comes into being nor leaves. Why then, Ashtavakra asks, do you grieve for what is only a passing form?
verse.for_you: You are sitting in the library, surrounded by the noise of other students, and the distance between you and them feels like a wall. This verse tells you that the body and the mind are temporary, but you are the awareness that watches them.
verse.scene_line: You are the library chair that holds you while the noise of the room comes and goes.
asks: How do I see myself when no one is watching?
Can I let the feeling of being an imposter pass without fighting it?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: On how the self is found.
verse.sanskrit: तिलेषु तैलं दधिनीव सर्पिरापः स्रोतःस्वरणीषु चाग्निः । एवमात्माऽत्मनि गृह्यतेऽसौसत्येनैनं तपसायोऽनुपश्यति ॥
verse.line: Like oil in sesame or butter in curd, what you seek is already within. Sincere effort brings it out.
verse.translation: As oil in sesame seeds, butter in curd, water in springs and fire in fire-sticks, so is the self found within oneself by one who seeks it with truth and discipline.
verse.meaning: A seer is telling a seeker how to find the self. The self is already inside you, just as oil is in sesame seeds or butter is in curd. You do not need to make it appear. You only need to look in the right way, with truth and steady discipline, to draw it out.
verse.for_you: You feel cut off because you think you could build a worthy self from nothing. The distance you feel is not a missing piece. It is the effort of looking outside for what is already inside. Let the self you are becoming rest in the self you already are.
verse.try_today: When you sit down to study, notice the feeling of being an imposter.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own kitchen, and the answer is already in the curd.
asks: How do I stop looking outside for what is already here?
Can I trust that I am enough before I finish my degree?

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: Follows the call to enjoy by letting go: how to live and work.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वन्नेवेह कर्माणि जिजीविषेच्छतꣳ समाः । एवं त्वयि नान्यथेतोऽस्ति न कर्म लिप्यते नरे ॥
verse.line: Do your work and wish to live a full hundred years. Done in this spirit, action does not cling.
verse.translation: Doing your work here, you may wish to live a hundred years. For you there is no other way than this: done in this spirit, action does not cling to a person.
verse.why: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

prasang.title: The Isha: enjoy by letting go
prasang.summary: Eighteen verses that open by saying everything belongs to the divine, so we should enjoy it without grasping. They go on to say we should work a full life without being bound, and see ourselves in all beings.
prasang.lesson: Hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.

verse.meaning: The seer is speaking to the reader about the rhythm of a working life. They say, do your work here, and you may wish to live a full hundred years. There is no other way than this. If you do it in this spirit, action does not cling to you. It means hold what you have lightly, keep working, and see yourself in everyone.
verse.for_you: You are studying, and the weight of it feels like it is only on your shoulders. The work is yours, but the outcome is not. Let your effort be the work, and let the results go. The people around you are not your rivals.
verse.try_today: Do one small task with full attention, and let the result go.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own study, holding the work lightly and letting the outcome go.
asks: How do I let go of the outcome without giving up?
What does it mean to see myself in my classmates?
Can I do the work without needing the result?

story.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
story.story_hook: Among all the guards, one of them wiped Sita's tears and told her the truth.
story.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
story.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

anchor.speaker: Sita
anchor.setting: A kind guard, Sarama, offers to spy for Sita; Sita asks only to know what is decided about her.
anchor.sanskrit: यदि नाम कथा तस्य निश्चितं वापि यद्भवेत्। निवेदयेथाः सर्वं तद्वरो मे स्यादनुग्रहः॥
anchor.line: Whatever has been decided, just tell me. Not knowing is the hardest part.
anchor.translation: If there is any talk about him, or anything decided at all, tell me everything. That would be the greatest kindness to me.
anchor.why: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

prasang.title: Sarama, a friend in the enemy's house
prasang.summary: Ravana tries to break Sita with a fake head of Ram. Sarama, a kind rakshasi guard, comforts her, tells her the truth, and offers to find out what is being planned. Sita asks only to be told whatever is decided.
prasang.story_hook: Among all the guards, one of them wiped Sita's tears and told her the truth.
prasang.lesson: One kind person can make an unbearable place bearable; knowing is easier than wondering.

story.hook_title: Among all of Sita's guards, one wiped her tears and told her the truth
story.teaser: Among all of Sita's guards, one wiped her tears and told her the truth
story.for_you: You are in a place where everyone around you feels like a guard. But Sarama, a rakshasi, chose to see Sita and offer the truth. One person who sees you and speaks plainly can make the waiting easier than the unknown. Let that truth be your guide today.
asks: Who is the Sarama in my own life right now?
What truth do I need to hear to stop wondering?
How do I offer that same clarity to someone else?
